summary: Loudoun County Attorney Leo Rogers is reported to have stated that a moratorium is not allowed in the Commonwealth of Virginia, but that a pause on legislative applications is allowed.
notes: Legislative applications are the discretionary ones, rezonings and special exceptions, as distinct from by-right or administrative review. The distinction appears to be the drafting theory behind the Loudoun pause. A neighboring Virginia city separately distinguishes a pause pending ordinance revision from a moratorium, described there as a total wipeout of one specific use.
confidence_note: No written opinion has been read and no Virginia Code section is cited in the source. This records reported advice, not a legal conclusion, and must not be relied on without counsel.
